newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia expects Bre-X, Barrick deal on Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia expects Bre-X, Barrick deal on Dec 4.

text.p: The Indonesian government said Tuesday it was expecting confirmation Wednesday of a deal between Canadian mining companies Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp. over the huge Busang gold find.

Umar Said, secretary general in the Mines and Energy Ministry, told reporters the two companies were still negotiating and that he expected a deal before a Dec. 4 deadline set by the Indonesian government expired.
"They have to have an agreement. It is up to them to find the solution. We expect they will report about the deal on Dec. 4," Umar said.
He made no mention of a separate bid by Canada's Placer Dome Inc. to partner with Bre-X in developing the find.

The government has advised Bre-X, the majority owner of the Busang gold find in East Kalimantan province, to go into partnership with Barrick to develop the mine and gave it the deadline to reach a deal.
The government has indicated it wants Barrick to own 75 percent of Busang, which is estimated to contain at least 47 million ounces of gold, with Bre-X holding 25 percent.

Placer Dome said in Vancouver on Monday that it wrote to the Indonesian government late last week telling Jakarta it wanted "to make a competitive offer" for a stake in the property after an Indonesian diplomat was quoted as saying such offers would be considered before the deadline. A copy of the letter was obtained by Reuters.

A Placer spokesman said the gold producer had received no response yet to the letter, and it was unclear whether the effort was enough to derail Barrick's deal. Neither Bre-X nor Barrick had any comment on Placer's announcement.
Placer revealed that it had been negotiating with Bre-X for two months and had discussed a "conditional offer" well in excess of Bre-X's current share price of C$17.75 ($13.15).
Placer said its talks with Bre-X were cut short by the Indonesian government's order for Bre-X to negotiate with Barrick.

"We were very disappointed to see the auction process pre-empted," said Placer Chief Executive John Willson. "We regret that the opportunity for Bre-X shareholders to determine the value of their holdings, and to exercise their natural right to determine their partner, was taken away."
Indonesia's Umar also confirmed the ministry had requested Bre-X and Barrick to consider giving the government a 10 percent stake in the find.
He said the government had not set a 10 percent holding for the state as a condition of any Barrick/Bre-X deal or stipulated from whose share the stake was to come.

Bre-X, meanwhile, appears to have staved off litigation by an Indonesian partner, Jusuf Merukh, who had threatened a $1.9 billion lawsuit against the Canadian firm in an ownership dispute over Busang.
Merukh, who claims he is entitled to 40 percent of the find, told Reuters on Monday he had postponed any legal action as his lawyers had begun negotiations with Bre-X. He gave no details.
